product_family: Quizlet is a consumer/education flashcard and study platform (free tier + Quizlet Plus subscription) with classroom features for teachers and students (Quizlet for Classes). It previously offered an AI tutor, Q-Chat, built on the OpenAI API, which has since been discontinued (as of mid-2025 per public reporting). No separate enterprise/API product tier or dedicated healthcare offering was found.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1 or Type 2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Quizlet has no dedicated trust center; extensive search of quizlet.com, help.quizlet.com, and third-party compliance trackers found no SOC 2 report, badge, or reference.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on any Quizlet-owned domain or in independent coverage.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found. No AI-governance certification referenced anywhere on Quizlet's site or help center, despite Quizlet shipping AI features (former Q-Chat tutor, Magic Notes, etc.).

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a HIPAA compliance program or BAA offering. Quizlet is a general consumer/education product, not a healthcare product, so HIPAA is likely out of scope rather than a gap.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found. Quizlet Plus billing is a small subscription flow; no PCI attestation is published, and payment processing is most likely handled by a third-party processor (unconfirmed).

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found; not a government-focused product.

privacy.ai_training_note: Whether Quizlet trains its own models on user-generated study content (flashcard sets, answers) is not confirmed by vendor-domain evidence. Quizlet's AI features (formerly Q-Chat, an AI tutor 'built with OpenAI's ChatGPT API' per Quizlet's own 2023 blog post title) rely on third-party model providers (OpenAI) rather than a Quizlet-trained model, based on available reporting; Q-Chat itself appears to have been discontinued (public reporting indicates it was no longer available as of mid-2025). No explicit AI-training opt-out mechanism or AI-specific data-use page was found.
privacy.data_region: Not confirmed publicly. Quizlet's GDPR help-center article describes transferring personal data from the EEA to the US using EU-Commission-approved mechanisms (Standard Contractual Clauses), implying primary data processing and storage in the United States.

security.name: Encryption in transit / at rest
security.value: Quizlet's privacy policy states Quizlet 'uses reasonable efforts to follow generally accepted industry standards to protect personal information submitted to it, both during transmission and after receipt.' This is a general best-efforts statement, not a specific encryption-standard disclosure (e.g. TLS 1.2+/AES-256).

security.name: Vulnerability / abuse reporting contact
security.value: A security contact email (security@quizlet.com) is referenced in Quizlet's privacy policy, suggesting Quizlet accepts security reports, but no public bug bounty program or responsible-disclosure page was found.

security.name: International data transfer mechanism
security.value: Quizlet's GDPR help-center article describes use of EU-Commission-approved transfer mechanisms, including Standard Contractual Clauses, for EEA-to-US transfers. The same article also references the EU-US and Swiss-US Privacy Shield Frameworks, which were invalidated (Schrems II, 2020) and later superseded by the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (2023); citing 'Privacy Shield' verbatim would be stale legacy language.

security.name: Trust center / compliance documentation portal
security.value: None found. No trust.quizlet.com, security.quizlet.com, or equivalent portal exists; no downloadable SOC 2 report, security whitepaper, or subprocessor list was located.

products.name: Quizlet (free)
products.data_scope: User-generated study sets, account/profile data, usage/study activity (some profile and activity data may be publicly visible per the product's social features).
products.notes: Primary consumer product; account creation via email or SSO (Google/Apple, unconfirmed specifics).

products.name: Quizlet Plus
products.data_scope: Same as free tier plus payment/billing data for subscription management.
products.notes: Adds AI-assisted study features (e.g. Magic Notes/summary tools per public reporting); billing handled by an unconfirmed third-party payment processor.

products.name: Quizlet for Classes / Teachers
products.data_scope: May include minor (K-12 student) data where used in schools; teacher-managed class rosters and student study activity.
products.notes: No dedicated COPPA/FERPA compliance page or Student Privacy Pledge signatory confirmation was found on Quizlet's own domain, despite the product's wide use in K-12 settings.

products.name: Q-Chat (AI tutor, discontinued)
products.category: AI feature, formerly built on OpenAI's API
products.notes: Publicly reported as launched in 2023 and no longer available as of mid-2025; not confirmed as currently offered.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium consumer subscription (Quizlet Plus); no visible enterprise/seat-based or API pricing tier was found.
compare.data_residency: Unconfirmed; evidence points to US-based processing with SCC-based EEA transfers.

flags: No trust center and no evidence of SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, or FedRAMP anywhere on Quizlet's own domain or in independent coverage. This is normal for a consumer-focused edtech product, but no compliance badges should be shown.

Possible stale legacy reference to the invalidated EU-US/Swiss-US 'Privacy Shield' framework in Quizlet's GDPR help article; Privacy Shield was struck down in 2020 and replaced by the EU-US Data Privacy Framework in 2023. This could be an outdated document rather than an active claim.
No confirmation found of COPPA/FERPA-specific compliance messaging or Student Privacy Pledge signatory status, despite Quizlet's significant use in K-12 classrooms.
AI-training posture (whether user-generated flashcard content is used to train Quizlet's own models, and whether any opt-out exists) is not documented in vendor-domain sources.
